surviving_claim: Within the fixed single-writer process-crash experiment, completed real primary generations can accumulate as a FIFO of retirement descriptors without waiting for earlier cleanup. Enqueue appends one dual-copy descriptor and touches at most the existing tail; reclaim touches only the committed head descriptor plus the explicit segment budget. The tested crash states are exact and recovery does not scan retirement history.
non_claims: Total retirement-descriptor storage is not constant; append-only descriptor history grows with completed generations.
The experiment does not establish hardware power-loss, torn-sector, drive-cache, or filesystem-journal guarantees.
The experiment does not establish arbitrary multi-writer or distributed correctness.
The fixed 64-bit logical-segment and physical-pointer namespaces are not mathematical unboundedness.
The experiment does not reclaim descriptor pages, empty radix metadata nodes, or filesystem blocks.
The real-primary queue depth exercised is three simultaneously retired generations; larger queue counts are arithmetic/control cases, not real exponential-capacity growth runs.
